title: Microsoft Teams: upgraded call history in the Calls app
summary: Hold: the route to Make private calls omits the Edit step that Microsoft instructs administrators to select before changing an existing calling policy. The rollout details, commands and default state are supported; smaller corrections concern licensing attribution, the voicemail route and retention guidance.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Users with Make private calls turned off in their calling policy cannot see the Calls app.
claims.quote: If the Make private calls setting is turned off in the calling policy, users with that policy can't see the Calls app in their Teams client

claims.claim: Make private calls controls all Teams calling functionality, not just the upgraded history.
claims.quote: Make private calls - This setting controls all calling capabilities in Teams. Turn this setting off to turn off all calling functionality in Teams.

claims.claim: Native Teams calling is turned on by policy for all users by default.
claims.quote: By default, Microsoft Teams native calling is turned on via policy for all users.

claims.claim: An administrator reaches Make private calls through Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Make private calls.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Microsoft Teams admin center, select Voice > Calling policies.
Select the policy or policies that you want to modify, and then select Edit.
claims.fix: Replace controls[0].ui.path and its rendered table path with 'Voice > Calling policies > policy > Edit > Make private calls'. The cited page requires selecting Edit after choosing the existing policy.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowPrivateCalling $false disables Teams calling in the Global policy.
claims.quote:
[-AllowPrivateCalling <boolean>]
Controls all calling capabilities in Teams. Turning this off will turn off all calling functionality in Teams.

claims.claim: An administrator reaches Voicemail for inbound calls through Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Voicemail for inbound calls.
claims.quote:
go to Voice > Calling Policies
Choose the policy you would like to update or select Add to create a new policy.
For Voicemail for inbound calls, select one of the following options:
claims.fix: The voicemail page supports the printed route, but https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/teams-calling-policy explicitly requires Edit for an existing policy. Replace controls[1].ui.path and its rendered path with 'Voice > Calling policies > policy > Edit > Voicemail for inbound calls', retaining both cited pages.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowVoicemail AlwaysDisabled disables inbound routing to voicemail in the Global policy.
claims.quote:
this script turns off the ability for users to route inbound calls to voicemail for the Global (default) Teams Calling Policy instance:
Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowVoicemail AlwaysDisabled

claims.claim: Voicemail for inbound calls governs routing to voicemail, rather than configuring the new history presentation.
claims.quote: You can control whether routing of calls to Cloud Voicemail is allowed for Teams users by using the Teams admin center or by using PowerShell.

claims.where: controls[2].ui, controls[2].api, controls[2].note; Why it matters; Governance controls; changes
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no tenant or user switch specifically enabling or disabling upgraded Calls app call history.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams upgraded call history enable disable Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy call history 570843. Opened teams-calling-policy, cloud-voice-landing-page and Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy; no upgrade switch. Shared Call History templates concern queues and auto attendants, not this upgrade.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe this personal Calls app history upgrade in a feature-specific page.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Calls app upgraded call history 3000 records 6 months policy setting licensing; Microsoft Teams upgraded call history missed calls associated voicemails consolidated single entry. Read results and calling overview: shared queue history and device updates, not this upgrade.

claims.claim: Administering the existing Teams calling policy settings requires a privileged Teams administration role.

claims.claim: Teams call log retention is managed through Microsoft Purview rather than the Teams admin center.
claims.quote:
This separate retention policy for call logs can be created and modified only by using PowerShell.
After you create the retention policy for Teams call logs, it's displayed in Data Lifecycle Management > Policies in the Microsoft Purview portal, where it's visible but read-only.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-retention-policies in sources and beside the sentence about where retention is managed. To make the surface unambiguous, replace that sentence with 'Teams call log retention policies are created and modified only with PowerShell and are visible but read-only in the Microsoft Purview portal.'

claims.claim: Every control the checklist asks administrators to check appears in the controls table.
claims.quote:
Confirm with your compliance team how Teams call logs are covered by your Microsoft Purview retention policies and eDiscovery practice
The table lists calling availability, inbound voicemail routing and an undocumented upgrade switch, but no retention control.
claims.fix: The Before rollout bullet asking readers to confirm coverage by Microsoft Purview retention policies has no corresponding controls row. Remove that checklist bullet; retain the already documented retention explanation and open question. Do not add a control row as part of this correction.
